comparisons.peer_summary: On November 22, 2023, Broadcom acquired VMware for a fair value of $53.4 billion using $30.4 billion in term loans and cash on hand, and subsequently sold VMware's end-user computing business to KKR for $3.5 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose significant capital allocation activities and financing strategies in Item 1, but differ in execution: Intel suspended dividends and share repurchases due to CHIPS Act restrictions and a focus on critical investments, whereas Broadcom actively engaged in a massive $53.4 billion acquisition of VMware funded by term loans and cash on hand. Intel's capital return was halted ("suspended the declaration of quarterly dividends starting with the fourth quarter of 2024"), while Broadcom executed large-scale capital deployment ("acquired VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction... with a fair value of $53.4 billion" and "funded the cash portion... with net proceeds from the issuance of $30.4 billion in term loans").

sentences.text: Our most recent stock repurchase was in the first quarter of 2021 and we suspended the declaration of quarterly dividends starting with the fourth quarter of 2024.

Further, we do not expect to pay dividends or make stock repurchases until our cash flows improve as we focus on the critical investments needed to execute our business strategy and create long-term value.

On November 22, 2023, we acquired VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction (the "VMware Merger"), in which VMware stockholders received, in aggregate, approximately $30.8 billion in cash and 544 million shares of Broadcom common stock (on a split adjusted basis) with a fair value of $53.4 billion.

We funded the cash portion of the VMware Merger consideration with net proceeds from the issuance of $30.4 billion in term loans under a credit agreement that we entered into on August 15, 2023, as well as cash on hand.
